fixes.answer: I would say it is not necessarily better, but far more convenient and personalised. Streaming and online platforms offer endless choice [[on demand]], which is [[hard to beat]]. However, traditional forms like cinema, live theatre or reading a physical book offer a certain quality and communal experience that online consumption can lack. So I appreciate the convenience, but I do not think it fully replaces the [[richness]] of certain traditional experiences.
fixes.why: 'replaces' and 'experiences' are plain; marked 'on demand' and 'hard to beat'

fixes.answer: Its popularity comes down to convenience and choice. Streaming offers instant, on-demand access to an enormous library of content that you can watch anywhere, anytime, without adverts. It is also relatively affordable compared to traditional cable. The personalised recommendations keep people engaged, and [[binge-watching]] entire series has become a [[cultural phenomenon]]. Essentially, it perfectly suits the modern desire for flexibility and [[instant gratification]].
fixes.why: 'engaged', 'flexibility', 'instant' are plain; marked 'binge-watching', 'cultural phenomenon', and the phrase 'instant gratification'

fixes.answer: The impact is genuinely mixed and often exaggerated. On the positive side, many games improve problem-solving, coordination and even teamwork when played socially, and they are a legitimate form of relaxation. However, excessive gaming can lead to addiction, a [[sedentary lifestyle]] and, in some cases, exposure to [[toxic]] online behaviour. So like most things, video games are beneficial [[in moderation]] but harmful to excess.
fixes.why: 'beneficial' and 'harmful' are plain; marked 'sedentary lifestyle' and 'in moderation'

fixes.answer: I expect entertainment to become far more [[immersive]] and interactive. Virtual and augmented reality could allow us to step inside stories and games rather than merely watching them. Artificial intelligence may create personalised content tailored precisely to individual tastes. The line between passive viewing and active participation will likely blur. While thrilling, I hope this does not come at the expense of the shared, communal joys that entertainment can [[foster]] and [[preserve]].

Self-discipline and awareness are key. Setting clear time limits and using apps that track usage can prevent hours from [[slipping away]] unnoticed. Consciously scheduling other activities, like exercise, hobbies or socialising, ensures entertainment does not [[crowd out]] everything else. It also helps to remove the [[constant temptation]], perhaps by keeping devices out of reach. Essentially, treating entertainment as a reward rather than a default keeps it in balance.
fixes.why: 4 marks with plain 'reward', 'balance', 'default'; kept sir's 'crowd out' and marked 'slipping away' and 'constant temptation'
